_note: Made by tools/build-lines.py from people.json and the lines TSVs; never typed. Counts only for anybody who may not be listed.
rule: Kin are the register's own links: father, mother, child, spouse, brother and sister. A link that rests only on a family tree is not followed, and a godparent, a witness, an official or a neighbour is not kin.

Following those links splits the register into family groups. A line holds every group that contains one of its seeds: a person on one of its dated stops, or a person the archive puts on it by an act it quotes (data/people-lines.tsv).

A group that holds the seeds of two lines is a join. It is allowed only where the archive records that join as documented, as it does for the direct line and the Taylor line, joined by the marriage of 1911; each person then goes to the line of the nearest seed, counted in links.

A group on no line is a household not yet placed. Where a household the archive has written up names one of its people, it is that household; otherwise it is counted as a household of its own when it holds two people or more and one of them carries the name.
Anyone on no line and in no household is counted in one of two pens: people of the name with no family recorded here, or people in the acts who are not of the name and are kin to nobody here.

Everybody is counted, and nobody is counted twice. A person is listed by name only when their page publishes a birth year before the living line or a death, and no rule of this archive holds them as living or out of publication; everybody else is a number only.

households.label: JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA — named at Buenos Aires, 1908
households.why: *** THE TWO THIS ARCHIVE EXISTS TO FIND, and the reason the red lane is drawn broken. *** They are named as the parents on Pablo Armando's army enrolment card and appear in NO OTHER RECORD ANYWHERE - not in Rosario, not in Montevideo, not in the full-text corpus. Every lane above is a candidate and none has been shown to hold them.

households.label: The LARENA of Gualeguaychu — Entre Rios, 1837-1913
households.why: The people in the register under the A-spelling at Gualeguaychu, in Entre Rios, the province across the Parana. *** THE SPELLING IS NOT THE PROBLEM - this archive has catalogued LERENA read as SERENA, LORENA, LESINA and six more. *** What is missing is any document joining them to a Uruguayan house. (The Larena of Cayasta, in Santa Fe, were drawn here with them until 27 October 2026; the archive's own correction says Cayasta was an Italian colony and its Larena not ours, so they are drawn with the different stock below.)

households.label: CARLOS LERENA of Mendoza — Mendoza, 1900-1904
households.why: Married ADELA CAMIGLIA; a son AVELINO CARLOS born 1904. *** The forename AVELINO is the one that runs through Sancho's house ***, which is suggestive and is not evidence. Worked in September and not joined.

households.label: The LERENA of Trinidad with no father named — Trinidad, Flores, 1895-1918
households.why: CAYETANA FAUSTINA, whose son Luis was registered in 1895 with no father on the act; RODOLFO BERNARDO and ISMAEL, each a father who appears once. *** Real people on real acts, attached to nobody. ***

households.label: LERINA — Italy, arrived 1889
households.why: Four people, arrived together in 1889 - Anna, Annunziata, Laurensa, Savina. *** An Italian name that is not a spelling of this one ***, kept in the register so that nobody has to discover them twice. (The register also holds two Italian arrivals written LERENA, Domenico in 1910 and Paolo in 1913, who are unplaced and not excluded.)

households.label: LERENA of Arequipa — Peru, 1797-1825
households.why: Felipa, Pedro and Isidoro Lerena in the parish marriages of Chuquibamba, Condesuyos. *** Found while searching the full-text corpus and recorded because a rare name in a far place is exactly what a careless session would merge. ***

households.label: The LERENA y LERENA of Navarrete — Logrono, Spain and Buenos Aires, 1900-1930
households.why: *** A WHOLE HOUSEHOLD WHO CARRY THE NAME TWICE, and the most useful namesake on this page. *** ISABELA LERENA y BASARAN, widow, of Navarrete in La Rioja; her sons JOSE DOLORES, married and the propietario at home, and PRUDENCIO BENITO and JUAN JOSE, bachelors and shop-assistants in Buenos Aires, who in November 1900 signed a power of attorney at the Spanish consulate putting the Spanish property in their mother's hands. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN HERE AND NOT ON A LANE: *** they are Spanish subjects out of Logrono, and the first two lanes above are Banda Oriental stock documented from the 1790s; the other three begin at Rosario, in Spain and in Spain, and no connection is claimed between this household and any of them. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN AT ALL: *** Pablo Armando's enrolment card names a JUAN CARLOS LERENA and a MARIA LERENA, and the easiest way to dismiss that card is to call the repeated surname a clerk's slip. *** AND THEY ARE THE SIXTH SUCH COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET, NOT THE FIRST - a correction to what was written here first. *** The two Trinidad couples of 1894 and 1913, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912 all came before them. *** SO THE CARD'S DOUBLE SURNAME WAS NEVER IN REAL DOUBT, AND NAVARRETE DOES NOT RESCUE IT. *** What Navarrete adds is different and smaller: it is the *** FIRST SUCH HOUSEHOLD OUTSIDE SOUTH AMERICA ***, the *** FIRST WHERE THE CHILDREN CARRY IT DOUBLED AS A SURNAME OF RECORD *** - 'Lerena y Lerena', in their own signatures, not just a coincidence of two parents - and the *** FIRST TIME THE PRACTICE HAS A PLACE ON A MAP *** that can be searched. It does not make them his - no connection is claimed, and the CEMLA arrivals suggest a steady traffic of young Riojan Lerena men into Buenos Aires shops that has nothing to do with Rosario de Santa Fe in 1882.

households.label: BENITO LERENA and MARIA CRISTINA — San Eugenio, Artigas, Uruguay, 1899
households.why: *** A Lerena household on the Brazilian border, found 12 October 2026 and not on any lane. *** Benito, b. about 1854, Oriental, a jornalero who could not sign his name; his wife Maria Cristina, b. about 1856, Brazilian, given no surname by the act; their daughter Anastasia LERENA, b. about 1877, married to the Brazilian soldier Honorio ALVAREZ. Artigas is a department this archive has never worked, and a family of the name sitting on the Brazil frontier with Brazilian-born children is a shape nothing here predicts. *** Found only because a LERENA father was asked against a SERENA mother - and the act turns out to say Lerena both times. ***

households.label: PEDRO LERENA and JUANA CAMACHO — Jesus Maria and Mal Abrigo, San Jose, Uruguay, 1910
households.why: *** An Italian-born Lerena in the department this archive rests an 1846 couple on. *** Pedro, b. about 1842 in Italy, a labrador; Juana Camacho, b. about 1853, Oriental; their daughter Ramona LERENA, b. about 1886, who registered a natural daughter Antonina at Mal Abrigo in September 1910 with the father's line left as se ignora. *** Kept here rather than on a lane, and kept as UNPLACED rather than as a namesake, because the honest position is that this archive cannot yet tell which stock he belongs to - which is itself the finding. *** /name/ separates an Italian Lerena/Lerina stock from this family; it has always been able to do that by country, and this act is the case where country does not decide.

households.label: LEANDRO LERENA and LUCIA LLANOS — Buenos Aires, 1895-1896
households.why: *** THE HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED AS A TRUE NULL, AND IT WAS NEVER ONE. *** Leandro, born about 1854-57 at SEGOVIA, an oil maker, literate; his wife Lucia Llanos; children Emilia (b. Spain c.1886), Francisco (b. La Plata c.1890), Paulina (b. 1895) and, on the baptism of San Cristobal on 20 December 1896, SALVADOR - the son whose army card spells the surname LORENA. Living at Calle Pichincha 929. *** A FOURTH SPANISH ARRIVAL beside the three the Spain lane already draws, and NOT SHOWN TO BE CONNECTED TO ANY OF THEM. *** Segovia is also outside the one Spanish cluster this archive can point to - La Rioja, at 39.6 times the national rate - which makes kinship with the Navarrete household less likely, not more. See /argentina/#s-leandro-llanos.

households.label: GIL LERENA and ANASTASIA SANTA CRUZ — Trinidad and Pintos, Flores
households.why: *** A SECOND LERENA HOUSE AT TRINIDAD, AND NOT ALEJANDRO'S. *** Gil Lerena was at Trinidad in the 1840s-60s and died in 1883 at sixty-four; his sons were Faustino (1844-1866) and Fermin, whose children run on to Pintos. *** He is not placed: no act names his parents, and nothing ties him to Alejandro's brothers or to Sancho's sons. ***

households.label: MAURICIO LERENA and PETRONA AGUILAR — La Guardia, Trinidad, 1866
households.why: A Mauricio Lerena with a wife Petrona Aguilar, godparents in February and March 1866 and the parents of Paula Gregoria, born 14 June 1866. *** He may be the Mauricio of Flores born about 1836, and he is not the Colla Mauricio, who had a wife Casimira. Not merged. ***

households.label: PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA and TERESA LEONARD — Montevideo, 1861-1901
households.why: *** NOT THE PEDRO LERENA VEGA WHO DIED IN 1896: *** the 1864 christening of their daughter Manuela names his parents as Pedro and Maria Pereyra. His father could be Pedro Antonio, son of Sancho, *** only if that man married a second wife, Maria Pereyra, after Vicenta Vega - which nothing says. ***

a.label: Out of Canelones, into Montevideo

b.label: Rosario de Santa Fe, to the Cape

joins.says: Hypothesis 1c, that the family came from Uruguay, not Argentina. For it: the Rosario baptism index, read end to end for 1731-1901, holds one Lerena, and he is a Lerena Lenguas of this house; and in the army drawer Cajon 985 every traceable father of a Lerena card is a Uruguayan family's son. Against it: no link has been shown between Luis Lerena Lenguas and Juan Carlos Lerena, and Juan Carlos is in none of the household's children. The story draws the break at Sancho's grandchildren and leaves it open.
joins.label: Hypothesis 1c: a Montevideo house, and no paper joins it to Juan Carlos

a.label: Rosario de Santa Fe, to the Cape

b.label: Devon to the Cape: the Taylor line, by marriage

joins.says: Pablo Armando Lerena married Mary Septima Taylor at St Dominic's, Wynberg, on 3 September 1911: entry 160 of the duplicate original register. The Taylor line is drawn as a lane of its own because this archive keeps it as one; the two meet at that act, and their children are counted on the direct line.

a.label: The house of Luis Lerena and Justiniana Lenguas

b.label: Out of Canelones, into Montevideo

joins.says: Three acts name Luis Lerena's parents as Sancho and Maria Fernandez: his own baptism of 10 February 1811, his second marriage of 3 March 1842 and his son Alberto Octavio's baptism of 7 October 1850. So the Lerena Lenguas household, Gilberto of the Argentine Stud Book among them, is Sancho's grandchildren. (The register's own link from Luis to Sancho is still marked as resting on a tree, and his row still says 'probably'.)

a.label: The Lerena Larriera of San Jose

b.label: Out of Canelones, into Montevideo

joins.says: Set aside as 'not ours' on 14 September 2026 and retracted on 21 September: Alberto Lerena's Montevideo death registration of 2 March 1921, read at the image, names his parents as Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel. The nine children of Alberto and Maria Ines Larriera are great-grandchildren of Sancho. A refusal the archive itself withdrew.

a.label: The Trinidad kindred, Alejandro's house

b.label: Out of Rosario del Colla, into Trinidad

joins.says: The Trinidad expedientes of 1855 and 1858 name Alejandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez as the parents of Socorro and Bernabe, and Ramon Lerena and Maria Gonzalez as their grandparents; Alejandro's own marriage of 16 September 1825, read at the plate, calls him the son of Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez. Ramon of Rosario-Colla is Ramon of the Trinidad diagram.

a.label: The house of Cipriano Lerena and Lauriana Beloqui

b.label: Out of Rosario del Colla, into Trinidad

joins.says: Held apart from the Colla house until 9 October 2026. The Flores birth act of his daughter Carmen Donata, 2 March 1895, has him name his wife and both his parents, Mauricio and Casimira Montano: so the Beloqui children are grandchildren of Mauricio of Colla. (The register does not yet draw his link to Mauricio; the line counts him by this act.)

a.label: Out of Rosario del Colla, into Trinidad

b.label: Out of Canelones, into Montevideo

joins.says: Whether the Trinidad kindred joins Sancho's house is an open question with no evidence either way, which is why no join is drawn between them.

a.label: Arturo Lerena Garcia: Spain, Chile, Entre Rios

b.label: Out of Canelones, into Montevideo

joins.says: On 13 September 2026 an Arturo Lerena born at Montevideo in 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel, was run together with the Arturo Lerena of the army drawer. That was two men: the Uruguayan record gives that Arturo's wife as Ema Regules, and the Arturo of the drawer married Amalia Diaz and had children in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios. The row was withdrawn the same evening.

a.label: Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena (married 1922)

b.label: Rosario de Santa Fe, to the Cape

joins.says: The only 'Juan Carlos Lerena' in FamilySearch's full text besides a 2001 death, checked and excluded on 15 September 2026: Lerena is his second surname, his mother's, and he married in 1922. Pablo Armando's father must carry Lerena as his father's name and have been born by about the 1850s. He stands on Ramon's line, by his mother.

a.label: LERINA — Italy, arrived 1889

b.label: Rosario de Santa Fe, to the Cape

joins.says: Hypothesis 1b, that the family was Italian and the name nearer LERINA: the four LERINA arrivals of 1889 remain excluded, on their dates and not on a judgement about the surname. The eldest was fifty-nine and the youngest seventeen when they landed, seven years after Pablo Armando was born.
